newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Feb real ind output contracts 5.8 pct yr/yr. [corrected 07:55 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Czech Feb real ind output contracts 5.8 pct yr/yr. [corrected 07:55 gmt]

text.p: Czech real final industrial production in February contracted by 5.8 percent, year-on-year, after a 13.3 percent rise in the same month of the previous year, the Statistical Bureau (CSU) said on Wednesday.

It added that average industrial monthly wages grew, in nominal terms, 11.4 (corrects from 14.4) percent, year-on-year, in February, after 14.4 percent growth in January. The CSU also said that real construction output for February contracted by 1.6 percent, year-on-year.
The CSU added that industrial sales for February, in real terms, eased by 3.6 percent, year-on-year.

NOTE. In January, the CSU changed its methodology for calculating industrial production. The new methodology excludes multiple calculation of semi-finished products, resources, and other materials and commodities, which were included in output data at every stage under the old method measuring the gross value of all goods produced. The new index measures output changes by units, weight or other measurements, of the total of 1,304 products out of 879 product groups consisting of one or more similar products.

The product groups's output indices are placed in sectors, using weighting equal to their weight in the respective industrial sector. The overall index is calculated from weighted changes in the sectoral indices.
The average nominal industrial wage in February was 9,222 crowns compared with 9,904 in January. The February index of real wages was up 3.8 percent.
